newsitem.title: USA: US stocks edge lower at midday in cautious trading.
newsitem.headline: US stocks edge lower at midday in cautious trading.

text.p: Wall Street stocks drifted slightly lower at midsession as mild profit-taking and investor caution ahead of Friday's September paryolls report kept prices in check.
The Dow Industrials were down 11 points to 5923. The Nasdaq Composite was one point lower at 1235 and the S&P 500 index eased two points to 692.
"I think we're seeing some profit-taking in here because many stocks, particularly techs, have gotten back to their highs," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
Volume was relatively light, with about 185 million shares traded on the NYSE. Stocks generally held to within narrow ranges throughout the morning.

With September payrolls, wages and unemployment data due tomorrow, analysts said investors appeared content to bide their time until issuance of the report, considered a key leading indicator for inflation.

Economists expect payrolls to rise 166,000 for the month, a considerably tamer rate of growth than the 250,000 increase in August. Average hourly earnings and the U.S. unemployment rate are expected to increase marginally.
Individual issues provided most of the action this morning, with a handful of names dominating the session.
"There continues to be some concentrated buying among Nasdaq big-cap names," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Cisco Systems Inc rose 1-1/8 to 65 and Intel Corp gained 1/4 to 99-1/4 after earlier reaching a year high 100-1/4, its first venture past the 100 milestone.
Monsanto Co jumped 2-1/2 to 41-1/8 after an analyst at PaineWebber predicted the company's third quarter earnings would pleasantly surprise Wall Street.
Investors continued to punish severely those companies whose earnings threaten to disappoint.
Wall Data Inc fell 7-3/4 to 15-1/2 after saying it expected to post a loss for the third quarter.
Peak Technologies Group Inc fell 8-1/2 to 13-1/4 and EIS International Inc fell 5-1/16 to 7-15/16. Both said their third quarter earnings would fall short of Wall Street estimates.
Profit-taking also afflicted the bond market, where the benchmark 30-year bond slipped 3/32, sending the yield to 6.85 percent.
Early in the session the long bond rose more than a quarter point, but it eventually succumbed to the same cautious selling that hit stocks just before midday.
